basics.name: Pedro Fontanarrosa
basics.label: Multidisciplinary Researcher & Software Engineer | Statistical Modeling & Data Standards
basics.summary: Multidisciplinary researcher with extensive experience in computational/software engineering and biological sciences with 7+ years executing end-to-end statistical workflows: experimental design support, analysis plan writing, data standards adoption, reproducible programming, and rigorous QC. Deep experience building analysis datasets and publication-grade TLFs in Python/R. Comfortable translating complex methods for non-statisticians and coordinating with cross‑functional teams across US/UK time zones.

Applied ML researcher turned engineer building reproducible modeling pipelines and data products. 7+ years owning end-to-end workflows: schema design, data prep, modeling/evaluation, CI/CD, and QC. Strong with Python, PyTorch/TensorFlow, PyMC, containers, and versioned artifacts; comfortable translating technical work into decisions across teams/time zones.

work.name: Computational Systems & Synthetic Biology Lab, University College London
highlights: Built reproducible Python pipelines turning noisy multi-omic time series into analysis-ready datasets with unit-tested transforms, imputation, and integrity checks; shipped publication-grade figures/TLFs tied to versioned code.

Owned evaluation harnesses and ablation matrices for physics-informed models; introduced deep ensembles and MC-dropout, materially improving accuracy and stability in synthetic gLV studies (e.g., M RMSE ↓ 1.152→0.021 via parameter scaling; µ RMSE ↓ ~54% via ensembles).
Containerized workflows (Docker) and instituted CI/CD (GitHub Actions) with artifact logging and run manifests for auditability and reproducibility across collaborators.
Partnered cross-functionally to translate modeling findings into decisions; presented methods and limitations to mixed technical/non-technical audiences.

work.name: Genetic Logic Lab, University of Colorado Boulder
highlights: Developed modeling pipelines to evaluate design robustness under noise/uncertainty; produced comparison reports and decision-support visuals.
Contributed to community data/metadata standards (SBOL/SBML/SED-ML), emphasizing validation rules, machine-readable exchange, and backward compatibility.
Maintained project administration artifacts (analysis notes, protocol-like docs, annotated shells) to ensure traceability across teams.

work.name: University of Utah
highlights: Designed and executed statistical modeling studies; ran simulation studies to assess estimator performance and robustness.
Stood up data processing/analysis pipelines with QA/QC via tests, reproducible environments, and version-controlled notebooks.
Mentored peers on experimental design, uncertainty analysis, and communicating results.

work.name: COMBINE Standards (SBOL Community)
highlights: Drafted/reviewed specification text for SBOL v3 enabling structured protocols and machine-readable model/metadata exchange; coordinated cross-institution contributors.

work.name: Data-Centric Biological Design & Engineering Interest Group (Alan Turing Institute)
highlights: Coordinated monthly seminar series (academia/industry); owned agendas, logistics, and stakeholder comms across US/UK time zones.
Standardized templates/checklists for abstracts/slides/summaries; maintained website/calendar with version control and auditability.

projects.name: MIMIC — Modeling & Inference of Microbiomes (Python, open source)
projects.description: Package integrating simulation (gLV/VAR/CR), Bayesian inference, and UQ with reproducible notebooks and docs.

projects.name: PINNs for Dynamics Inference
projects.description: Physics-informed neural networks to infer interpretable interaction parameters with ablations and UQ (ensembles, MC-dropout); comprehensive diagnostics.
